06.a4708abe00:
<n>62:2</n> Deus, Deus meus, * ad te de luce vígilo.
<n>62:2</n> Sitívit in te ánima mea, * quam multiplíciter tibi caro mea.
<n>62:3</n> In terra desérta, et ínvia, et inaquósa: * sic in sancto appárui tibi, ut vidérem virtútem tuam, et glóriam tuam.
<n>62:4</n> Quóniam mélior est misericórdia tua super vitas: * lábia mea laudábunt te.
<n>62:5</n> Sic benedícam te in vita mea: * et in nómine tuo levábo manus meas.
<n>62:6</n> Sicut ádipe et pinguédine repleátur ánima mea: * et lábiis exsultatiónis laudábit os meum.
<n>62:7</n> Si memor fui tui super stratum meum, in matutínis meditábor in te: * quia fuísti adjútor meus.
<n>62:8</n> Et in velaménto alárum tuárum exsultábo, adhǽsit ánima mea post te: * me suscépit déxtera tua.
<n>62:10</n> Ipsi vero in vanum quæsiérunt ánimam meam, introíbunt in inferióra terræ: * tradéntur in manus gládii, partes vúlpium erunt.
<n>62:12</n> Rex vero lætábitur in Deo, laudabúntur omnes qui jurant in eo: * quia obstrúctum est os loquéntium iníqua.
06.952ccea0f6:
<n>62:2</n> O God, my God, * to thee do I watch at break of day.
<n>62:2</n> For thee my soul hath thirsted; * for thee my flesh, O how many ways!
<n>62:3</n> In a desert land, and where there is no way, and no water: * so in the sanctuary have I come before thee, to see thy power and thy glory.
<n>62:4</n> For thy mercy is better than lives: * thee my lips shall praise.
<n>62:5</n> Thus will I bless thee all my life long: * and in thy name I will lift up my hands.
<n>62:6</n> Let my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness: * and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips.
<n>62:7</n> If I have remembered thee upon my bed, I will meditate on thee in the morning: * because thou hast been my helper.
<n>62:8</n> And I will rejoice under the covert of thy wings: my soul hath stuck close to thee: * thy right hand hath received me.
<n>62:10</n> But they have sought my soul in vain, they shall go into the lower parts of the earth: * they shall be delivered into the hands of the sword, they shall be the portions of foxes.
<n>62:12</n> But the king shall rejoice in God, all they shall be praised that swear by him: * because the mouth is stopped of them that speak wicked things.
06.8568f8555a:
<n>64:2</n> Te decet hymnus, Deus, in Sion: * et tibi reddétur votum in Jerúsalem.
<n>64:3</n> Exáudi oratiónem meam: * ad te omnis caro véniet.
<n>64:4</n> Verba iniquórum prævaluérunt super nos: * et impietátibus nostris tu propitiáberis.
<n>64:5</n> Beátus, quem elegísti, et assumpsísti: * inhabitábit in átriis tuis.
<n>64:5</n> Replébimur in bonis domus tuæ: * sanctum est templum tuum, mirábile in æquitáte.
<n>64:6</n> Exáudi nos, Deus, salutáris noster, * spes ómnium fínium terræ, et in mari longe.
<n>64:7</n> Prǽparans montes in virtúte tua, accínctus poténtia: * qui contúrbas profúndum maris sonum flúctuum ejus.
<n>64:8</n> Turbabúntur gentes, et timébunt qui hábitant términos a signis tuis: * éxitus matutíni, et véspere delectábis.
<n>64:10</n> Visitásti terram, et inebriásti eam: * multiplicásti locupletáre eam.
<n>64:10</n> Flumen Dei replétum est aquis, parásti cibum illórum: * quóniam ita est præparátio ejus.
<n>64:11</n> Rivos ejus inébria, multíplica genímina ejus: * in stillicídiis ejus lætábitur gérminans.
<n>64:12</n> Benedíces corónæ anni benignitátis tuæ: * et campi tui replebúntur ubertáte.
<n>64:13</n> Pinguéscent speciósa desérti: * et exsultatióne colles accingéntur.
<n>64:14</n> Indúti sunt aríetes óvium, et valles abundábunt fruménto: * clamábunt, étenim hymnum dicent.
06.9e0ba6bff9:
<n>64:2</n> A hymn, O God, becometh thee in Sion: * and a vow shall be paid to thee in Jerusalem.
<n>64:3</n> O hear my prayer: * all flesh shall come to thee.
<n>64:4</n> The words of the wicked have prevailed over us: * and thou wilt pardon our transgressions.
<n>64:5</n> Blessed is he whom thou hast chosen and taken to thee: * he shall dwell in thy courts.
<n>64:5</n> We shall be filled with the good things of thy house; holy is thy temple, * wonderful in justice.
<n>64:6</n> Hear us, O God our saviour, * who art the hope of all the ends of the earth, and in the sea afar off.
<n>64:7</n> Thou who preparest the mountains by thy strength, being girded with power: * who troublest the depth of the sea, the noise of its waves.
<n>64:8</n> The Gentiles shall be troubled, and they that dwell in the uttermost borders shall be afraid at thy signs: * thou shalt make the outgoings of the morning and of the evening to be joyful.
<n>64:10</n> Thou hast visited the earth, and hast plentifully watered it; * thou hast many ways enriched it.
<n>64:10</n> The river of God is filled with water, thou hast prepared their food; * for so is its preparation.
<n>64:11</n> Fill up plentifully the streams thereof, multiply its fruits; * it shall spring up and rejoice in its showers.
<n>64:12</n> Thou shalt bless the crown of the year of thy goodness: * and thy fields shall be filled with plenty.
<n>64:13</n> The beautiful places of the wilderness shall grow fat: * and the hills shall be girded about with joy.
<n>64:14</n> The rams of the flock are clothed, and the vales shall abound with corn: * they shall shout, yea they shall sing a hymn.
06.5131872438:
<n>66:2</n> Deus misereátur nostri, et benedícat nobis: * illúminet vultum suum super nos, et misereátur nostri.
<n>66:3</n> Ut cognoscámus in terra viam tuam, * in ómnibus géntibus salutáre tuum.
<n>66:4</n> Confiteántur tibi pópuli, Deus: * confiteántur tibi pópuli omnes.
<n>66:5</n> Læténtur et exsúltent gentes: * quóniam júdicas pópulos in æquitáte, et gentes in terra dírigis.
<n>66:6</n> Confiteántur tibi pópuli, Deus, confiteántur tibi pópuli omnes: * terra dedit fructum suum.
<n>66:7</n> Benedícat nos Deus, Deus noster, benedícat nos Deus: * et métuant eum omnes fines terræ.
06.fdc9255c27:
<n>66:2</n> May God have mercy on us, and bless us: * may he cause the light of his countenance to shine upon us, and may he have mercy on us.
<n>66:3</n> That we may know thy way upon earth: * thy salvation in all nations.
<n>66:4</n> Let people confess to thee, O God: * let all people give praise to thee.
<n>66:5</n> Let the nations be glad and rejoice: * for thou judgest the people with justice, and directest the nations upon earth.
<n>66:6</n> Let the people, O God, confess to thee: * let all the people give praise to thee: the earth hath yielded her fruit.
<n>66:7</n> May God, our God bless us, may God bless us: * and all the ends of the earth fear him.
06.bed93cb083:
<n>60:2</n> Exáudi, Deus, deprecatiónem meam: * inténde oratióni meæ.
<n>60:3</n> A fínibus terræ ad te clamávi: * dum anxiarétur cor meum, in petra exaltásti me.
<n>60:4</n> Deduxísti me, quia factus es spes mea: * turris fortitúdinis a fácie inimíci.
<n>60:5</n> Inhabitábo in tabernáculo tuo in sǽcula: * prótegar in velaménto alárum tuárum.
<n>60:6</n> Quóniam tu, Deus meus, exaudísti oratiónem meam: * dedísti hereditátem timéntibus nomen tuum.
<n>60:7</n> Dies super dies regis adícies: * annos ejus usque in diem generatiónis et generatiónis.
<n>60:8</n> Pérmanet in ætérnum in conspéctu Dei: * misericórdiam et veritátem ejus quis requíret?
<n>60:9</n> Sic psalmum dicam nómini tuo in sǽculum sǽculi: * ut reddam vota mea de die in diem.
06.9375e9cd8c:
<n>60:2</n> Hear, O God, my supplication: * be attentive to my prayer.
<n>60:3</n> To thee have I cried from the ends of the earth: * when my heart was in anguish, thou hast exalted me on a rock.
<n>60:4</n> Thou hast conducted me; for thou hast been my hope: * a tower of strength against the face of the enemy.
<n>60:5</n> In thy tabernacle I shall dwell for ever: * I shall be protected under the covert of thy wings.
<n>60:6</n> For thou, my God, hast heard my prayer: * thou hast given an inheritance to them that fear thy name.
<n>60:7</n> Thou wilt add days to the days of the king: * his years even to generation and generation.
<n>60:8</n> He abideth for ever in the sight of God: * his mercy and truth who shall search?
<n>60:9</n> So will I sing a psalm to thy name for ever and ever: * that I may pay my vows from day to day.
06.e307046dcf:
<n>61:2</n> Nonne Deo subjécta erit ánima mea? * ab ipso enim salutáre meum.
<n>61:3</n> Nam et ipse Deus meus, et salutáris meus: * suscéptor meus, non movébor ámplius.
<n>61:4</n> Quoúsque irrúitis in hóminem? * interfícitis univérsi vos: tamquam paríeti inclináto et macériæ depúlsæ?
<n>61:5</n> Verúmtamen prétium meum cogitavérunt repéllere, cucúrri in siti: * ore suo benedicébant, et corde suo maledicébant.
<n>61:6</n> Verúmtamen Deo subjécta esto, ánima mea: * quóniam ab ipso patiéntia mea.
<n>61:7</n> Quia ipse Deus meus, et salvátor meus: * adjútor meus, non emigrábo.
<n>61:8</n> In Deo salutáre meum, et glória mea: * Deus auxílii mei, et spes mea in Deo est.
<n>61:9</n> Speráte in eo omnis congregátio pópuli, effúndite coram illo corda vestra: * Deus adjútor noster in ætérnum.
<n>61:10</n> Verúmtamen vani fílii hóminum, mendáces fílii hóminum in statéris: * ut decípiant ipsi de vanitáte in idípsum.
<n>61:11</n> Nolíte speráre in iniquitáte, et rapínas nolíte concupíscere: * divítiæ si áffluant, nolíte cor appónere.
<n>61:12</n> Semel locútus est Deus, duo hæc audívi, quia potéstas Dei est, et tibi, Dómine, misericórdia: * quia tu reddes unicuíque juxta ópera sua.
06.7053eff73c:
<n>61:2</n> Shall not my soul be subject to God? * for from him is my salvation.
<n>61:3</n> For he is my God and my saviour: * he is my protector, I shall be moved no more.
<n>61:4</n> How long do you rush in upon a man? * you all kill, as if you were thrusting down a leaning wall, and a tottering fence.
<n>61:5</n> But they have thought to cast away my price; I ran in thirst: * they blessed with their mouth, but cursed with their heart.
<n>61:6</n> But be thou, O my soul, subject to God: * for from him is my patience.
<n>61:7</n> For he is my God and my saviour: * he is my helper, I shall not be moved.
<n>61:8</n> In God is my salvation and my glory: * he is the God of my help, and my hope is in God.
<n>61:9</n> Trust in him, all ye congregation of people: pour out your hearts before him. * God is our helper for ever.
<n>61:10</n> But vain are the sons of men, the sons of men are liars in the balances: * that by vanity they may together deceive.
<n>61:11</n> Trust not in iniquity, and cover not robberies: * if riches abound, set not your heart upon them.
<n>61:12</n> God hath spoken once, these two things have I heard, that power belongeth to God, and mercy to thee, O Lord; * for thou wilt render to every man according to his works.
06.5b1c3fbddc:
<n>65:1</n> Jubiláte Deo, omnis terra, psalmum dícite nómini ejus: * date glóriam laudi ejus.
<n>65:3</n> Dícite Deo: Quam terribília sunt ópera tua, Dómine! * in multitúdine virtútis tuæ mentiéntur tibi inimíci tui.
<n>65:4</n> Omnis terra adóret te, et psallat tibi: * psalmum dicat nómini tuo.
<n>65:5</n> Veníte, et vidéte ópera Dei: * terríbilis in consíliis super fílios hóminum.
<n>65:6</n> Qui convértit mare in áridam, in flúmine pertransíbunt pede: * ibi lætábimur in ipso.
<n>65:7</n> Qui dominátur in virtúte sua in ætérnum, óculi ejus super gentes respíciunt: * qui exásperant non exalténtur in semetípsis.
<n>65:8</n> Benedícite, gentes, Deum nostrum: * et audítam fácite vocem laudis ejus,
<n>65:9</n> Qui pósuit ánimam meam ad vitam: * et non dedit in commotiónem pedes meos.
<n>65:10</n> Quóniam probásti nos, Deus: * igne nos examinásti, sicut examinátur argéntum.
<n>65:11</n> Induxísti nos in láqueum, posuísti tribulatiónes in dorso nostro: * imposuísti hómines super cápita nostra.
<n>65:12</n> Transívimus per ignem et aquam: * et eduxísti nos in refrigérium.
06.9c7ab89434:
<n>65:1</n> Shout with joy to God, all the earth, sing ye a psalm to his name; * give glory to his praise.
<n>65:3</n> Say unto God, How terrible are thy works, O Lord! * in the multitude of thy strength thy enemies shall lie to thee.
<n>65:4</n> Let all the earth adore thee, * and sing to thee: let it sing a psalm to thy name.
<n>65:5</n> Come and see the works of God; * who is terrible in his counsels over the sons of men.
<n>65:6</n> Who turneth the sea into dry land, in the river they shall pass on foot: * there shall we rejoice in him.
<n>65:7</n> Who by his power ruleth for ever: his eyes behold the nations; * let not them that provoke him be exalted in themselves.
<n>65:8</n> O bless our God, ye Gentiles: * and make the voice of his praise to be heard.
<n>65:9</n> Who hath set my soul to live: * and hath not suffered my feet to be moved:
<n>65:10</n> For thou, O God, hast proved us: * thou hast tried us by fire, as silver is tried.
<n>65:11</n> Thou hast brought us into a net, thou hast laid afflictions on our back: * thou hast set men over our heads.
<n>65:12</n> We have passed through fire and water, * and thou hast brought us out into a refreshment.
06.015a567b22:
<n>65:13</n> Introíbo in domum tuam in holocáustis: * reddam tibi vota mea, quæ distinxérunt lábia mea.
<n>65:14</n> Et locútum est os meum, * in tribulatióne mea.
<n>65:15</n> Holocáusta medulláta ófferam tibi cum incénso aríetum: * ófferam tibi boves cum hircis.
<n>65:16</n> Veníte, audíte, et narrábo, omnes, qui timétis Deum: * quanta fecit ánimæ meæ.
<n>65:17</n> Ad ipsum ore meo clamávi, * et exaltávi sub lingua mea.
<n>65:18</n> Iniquitátem si aspéxi in corde meo, * non exáudiet Dóminus.
<n>65:19</n> Proptérea exaudívit Deus, * et atténdit voci deprecatiónis meæ.
<n>65:20</n> Benedíctus Deus, * qui non amóvit oratiónem meam, et misericórdiam suam a me.
06.e7cac612c8:
<n>65:13</n> I will go into thy house with burnt offerings: * I will pay thee my vows, which my lips have uttered,
<n>65:14</n> And my mouth hath spoken, * when I was in trouble.
<n>65:15</n> I will offer up to thee holocausts full of marrow, with burnt offerings of rams: * I will offer to thee bullocks with goats.
<n>65:16</n> Come and hear, all ye that fear God, * and I will tell you what great things he hath done for my soul.
<n>65:17</n> I cried to him with my mouth: * and I extolled him with my tongue.
<n>65:18</n> If I have looked at iniquity in my heart, * the Lord will not hear me.
<n>65:19</n> Therefore hath God heard me, * and hath attended to the voice of my supplication.
<n>65:20</n> Blessed be God, * who hath not turned away my prayer, nor his mercy from me.
06.391de74f76:
<n>67:2</n> Exsúrgat Deus, et dissipéntur inimíci ejus, * et fúgiant qui odérunt eum, a fácie ejus.
<n>67:3</n> Sicut déficit fumus, defíciant: * sicut fluit cera a fácie ignis, sic péreant peccatóres a fácie Dei.
<n>67:4</n> Et justi epuléntur, et exsúltent in conspéctu Dei: * et delecténtur in lætítia.
<n>67:5</n> Cantáte Deo, psalmum dícite nómini ejus: * iter fácite ei, qui ascéndit super occásum: <n>(fit reverentia)</n> Dóminus nomen illi.
<n>67:5</n> Exsultáte in conspéctu ejus: * turbabúntur a fácie ejus, patris orphanórum et júdicis viduárum.
<n>67:6</n> Deus in loco sancto suo: * Deus, qui inhabitáre facit uníus moris in domo:
<n>67:7</n> Qui edúcit vinctos in fortitúdine, * simíliter eos qui exásperant, qui hábitant in sepúlcris.
<n>67:8</n> Deus, cum egrederéris in conspéctu pópuli tui, * cum pertransíres in desérto:
<n>67:9</n> Terra mota est, étenim cæli distillavérunt a fácie Dei Sínai, * a fácie Dei Israël.
<n>67:10</n> Plúviam voluntáriam segregábis, Deus, hereditáti tuæ: * et infirmáta est, tu vero perfecísti eam.
<n>67:11</n> Animália tua habitábunt in ea: * parásti in dulcédine tua páuperi, Deus.
06.f489b75e03:
<n>67:2</n> Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered: * and let them that hate him flee from before his face.
<n>67:3</n> As smoke vanisheth, so let them vanish away: * as wax melteth before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God.
<n>67:4</n> And let the just feast, and rejoice before God: * and be delighted with gladness.
<n>67:5</n> Sing ye to God, sing a psalm to his name, * make a way for him who ascendeth upon the west: <n>(bow head)</n> the Lord is his name.
<n>67:5</n> Rejoice ye before him: * but the wicked shall be troubled at his presence, who is the father of orphans, and the judge of widows.
<n>67:6</n> God in his holy place: * God who maketh men of one manner to dwell in a house:
<n>67:7</n> Who bringeth out them that were bound in strength; * in like manner them that provoke, that dwell in sepulchres.
<n>67:8</n> O God, when thou didst go forth in the sight of thy people, * when thou didst pass through the desert:
<n>67:9</n> The earth was moved, and the heavens dropped at the presence of the God of Sinai, * at the presence of the God of Israel.
<n>67:10</n> Thou shalt set aside for thy inheritance a free rain, * O God: and it was weakened, but thou hast made it perfect.
<n>67:11</n> In it shall thy animals dwell; * in thy sweetness, O God, thou hast provided for the poor.
06.145f897804:
<n>67:12</n> Dóminus dabit verbum evangelizántibus, * virtúte multa.
<n>67:13</n> Rex virtútum dilécti, dilécti: * et speciéi domus divídere spólia.
<n>67:14</n> Si dormiátis inter médios cleros, pennæ colúmbæ deargentátæ, * et posterióra dorsi ejus in pallóre auri.
<n>67:15</n> Dum discérnit cæléstis reges super eam, nive dealbabúntur in Selmon: * mons Dei, mons pinguis.
<n>67:16</n> Mons coagulátus, mons pinguis: * ut quid suspicámini montes coagulátos?
<n>67:17</n> Mons, in quo beneplácitum est Deo habitáre in eo: * étenim Dóminus habitábit in finem.
<n>67:18</n> Currus Dei decem míllibus múltiplex, míllia lætántium: * Dóminus in eis in Sina in sancto.
<n>67:19</n> Ascendísti in altum, cepísti captivitátem: * accepísti dona in homínibus.
<n>67:19</n> Étenim non credéntes, * inhabitáre Dóminum Deum.
<n>67:20</n> Benedíctus Dóminus die cotídie: * prósperum iter fáciet nobis Deus salutárium nostrórum.
<n>67:21</n> Deus noster, Deus salvos faciéndi: * et Dómini Dómini éxitus mortis.
<n>67:22</n> Verúmtamen Deus confrínget cápita inimicórum suórum: * vérticem capílli perambulántium in delíctis suis.
<n>67:23</n> Dixit Dóminus: Ex Basan convértam, * convértam in profúndum maris:
<n>67:24</n> Ut intingátur pes tuus in sánguine: * lingua canum tuórum ex inimícis, ab ipso.
06.a339f168d2:
<n>67:12</n> The Lord shall give the word to them that preach good tidings, * with great power.
<n>67:13</n> The king of powers is of the beloved, * of the beloved; and the beauty of the house shall divide spoils.
<n>67:14</n> If you sleep among the midst of lots, you shall be as the wings of a dove covered with silver, * and the hinder parts of her back with the paleness of gold.
<n>67:15</n> When he that is in heaven appointeth kings over her, they shall be whited with snow in Selmon. * The mountain of God is a fat mountain,
<n>67:16</n> a curdled mountain, a fat mountain; * Why suspect, ye curdled mountains?
<n>67:17</n> A mountain in which God is well pleased to dwell: * for there the Lord shall dwell unto the end.
<n>67:18</n> The chariot of God is attended by ten thousands; thousands of them that rejoice: * the Lord is among them in Sinai, in the holy place.
<n>67:19</n> Thou hast ascended on high, thou hast led captivity captive; * thou hast received gifts in men.
<n>67:19</n> Yea for those also that do not believe, * the dwelling of the Lord God.
<n>67:20</n> Blessed be the Lord day by day: * the God of our salvation will make our journey prosperous to us.
<n>67:21</n> Our God is the God of salvation: * and of the Lord, of the Lord are the issues from death.
<n>67:22</n> But God shall break the heads of his enemies: * the hairy crown of them that walk on in their sins.
<n>67:23</n> The Lord said: I will turn them from Basan, * I will turn them into the depth of the sea:
<n>67:24</n> That thy foot may be dipped in the blood of thy enemies; * the tongue of thy dogs be red with the same.
06.87e7ede08d:
<n>67:25</n> Vidérunt ingréssus tuos, Deus: * ingréssus Dei mei: regis mei qui est in sancto.
<n>67:26</n> Prævenérunt príncipes conjúncti psalléntibus: * in médio juvenculárum tympanistriárum.
<n>67:27</n> In ecclésiis benedícite Deo Dómino, * de fóntibus Israël.
<n>67:28</n> Ibi Bénjamin adolescéntulus: * in mentis excéssu.
<n>67:28</n> Príncipes Juda, duces eórum: * príncipes Zábulon, príncipes Néphtali.
<n>67:29</n> Manda, Deus, virtúti tuæ: * confírma hoc, Deus, quod operátus es in nobis.
<n>67:30</n> A templo tuo in Jerúsalem, * tibi ófferent reges múnera.
<n>67:31</n> Íncrepa feras arúndinis, congregátio taurórum in vaccis populórum: * ut exclúdant eos, qui probáti sunt argénto.
<n>67:31</n> Díssipa gentes, quæ bella volunt: vénient legáti ex Ægýpto: * Æthiópia prævéniet manus ejus Deo.
<n>67:33</n> Regna terræ, cantáte Deo: * psállite Dómino.
<n>67:33</n> Psállite Deo, qui ascéndit super cælum cæli, * ad Oriéntem.
<n>67:34</n> Ecce dabit voci suæ vocem virtútis, date glóriam Deo super Israël, * magnificéntia ejus, et virtus ejus in núbibus.
<n>67:36</n> Mirábilis Deus in sanctis suis, Deus Israël ipse dabit virtútem, et fortitúdinem plebi suæ, * benedíctus Deus.
06.d0b4bd6bd2:
<n>67:25</n> They have seen thy goings, O God, * the goings of my God: of my king who is in his sanctuary.
<n>67:26</n> Princes went before joined with singers, * in the midst of young damsels playing on timbrels.
<n>67:27</n> In the churches bless ye God the Lord, * from the fountains of Israel.
<n>67:28</n> There is Benjamin a youth, * in ecstasy of mind.
<n>67:28</n> The princes of Juda are their leaders: * the princes of Zabulon, the princes of Nephthali.
<n>67:29</n> Command thy strength, O God: * confirm, O God, what thou hast wrought in us.
<n>67:30</n> From thy temple in Jerusalem, * kings shall offer presents to thee.
<n>67:31</n> Rebuke the wild beasts of the reeds, the congregation of bulls with the kine of the people; * who seek to exclude them who are tried with silver.
<n>67:31</n> Scatter thou the nations that delight in wars: ambassadors shall come out of Egypt: * Ethiopia shall soon stretch out her hands to God.
<n>67:33</n> Sing to God, ye kingdoms of the earth: * sing ye to the Lord:
<n>67:33</n> Sing ye to God, who mounteth above the heaven of heavens, * to the east.
<n>67:34</n> Behold he will give to his voice the voice of power: give ye glory to God for Israel, * his magnificence, and his power is in the clouds.
<n>67:36</n> God is wonderful in his saints: the God of Israel is he who will give power and strength to his people; * blessed be God.
06.6dbd59a477:
<n>68:2</n> Salvum me fac, Deus: * quóniam intravérunt aquæ usque ad ánimam meam.
<n>68:3</n> Infíxus sum in limo profúndi: * et non est substántia.
<n>68:3</n> Veni in altitúdinem maris: * et tempéstas demérsit me.
<n>68:4</n> Laborávi clamans, raucæ factæ sunt fauces meæ: * defecérunt óculi mei, dum spero in Deum meum.
<n>68:5</n> Multiplicáti sunt super capíllos cápitis mei, * qui odérunt me gratis.
<n>68:5</n> Confortáti sunt qui persecúti sunt me inimíci mei injúste: * quæ non rápui, tunc exsolvébam.
<n>68:6</n> Deus, tu scis insipiéntiam meam: * et delícta mea a te non sunt abscóndita.
<n>68:7</n> Non erubéscant in me qui exspéctant te, Dómine, * Dómine virtútum.
<n>68:7</n> Non confundántur super me * qui quærunt te, Deus Israël.
<n>68:8</n> Quóniam propter te sustínui oppróbrium: * opéruit confúsio fáciem meam.
<n>68:9</n> Extráneus factus sum frátribus meis, * et peregrínus fíliis matris meæ.
<n>68:10</n> Quóniam zelus domus tuæ comédit me: * et oppróbria exprobrántium tibi cecidérunt super me.
<n>68:11</n> Et opérui in jejúnio ánimam meam: * et factum est in oppróbrium mihi.
<n>68:12</n> Et pósui vestiméntum meum cilícium: * et factus sum illis in parábolam.
<n>68:13</n> Advérsum me loquebántur, qui sedébant in porta: * et in me psallébant qui bibébant vinum.
<n>68:13</n> Ego vero oratiónem meam ad te, Dómine: * tempus benepláciti, Deus.
06.63c32578ad:
<n>68:2</n> Save me, O God: * for the waters are come in even unto my soul.
<n>68:3</n> I stick fast in the mire of the deep: * and there is no sure standing.
<n>68:3</n> I am come into the depth of the sea: * and a tempest hath overwhelmed me.
<n>68:4</n> I have laboured with crying; my jaws are become hoarse: * my eyes have failed, whilst I hope in my God.
<n>68:5</n> They are multiplied above the hairs of my head, * who hate me without cause.
<n>68:5</n> My enemies are grown strong who have wrongfully persecuted me: * then did I pay that which I took not away.
<n>68:6</n> O God, thou knowest my foolishness; * and my offences are not hidden from thee.
<n>68:7</n> Let not them be ashamed for me, who look for thee, O Lord, * the Lord of hosts.
<n>68:7</n> Let them not be confounded on my account, * who seek thee, O God of Israel.
<n>68:8</n> Because for thy sake I have borne reproach; * shame hath covered my face.
<n>68:9</n> I am become a stranger to my brethren, * and an alien to the sons of my mother.
<n>68:10</n> For the zeal of thy house hath eaten me up: * and the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me.
<n>68:11</n> And I covered my soul in fasting: * and it was made a reproach to me.
<n>68:12</n> And I made haircloth my garment: * and I became a byword to them.
<n>68:13</n> They that sat in the gate spoke against me: * and they that drank wine made me their song.
<n>68:13</n> But as for me, my prayer is to thee, O Lord; * for the time of thy good pleasure, O God.
06.58658073b2:
<n>68:14</n> In multitúdine misericórdiæ tuæ exáudi me, * in veritáte salútis tuæ:
<n>68:15</n> Éripe me de luto, ut non infígar: * líbera me ab iis, qui odérunt me, et de profúndis aquárum.
<n>68:16</n> Non me demérgat tempéstas aquæ, neque absórbeat me profúndum: * neque úrgeat super me púteus os suum.
<n>68:17</n> Exáudi me, Dómine, quóniam benígna est misericórdia tua: * secúndum multitúdinem miseratiónum tuárum réspice in me.
<n>68:18</n> Et ne avértas fáciem tuam a púero tuo: * quóniam tríbulor, velóciter exáudi me.
<n>68:19</n> Inténde ánimæ meæ, et líbera eam: * propter inimícos meos éripe me.
<n>68:20</n> Tu scis impropérium meum, et confusiónem meam, * et reveréntiam meam.
<n>68:21</n> In conspéctu tuo sunt omnes qui tríbulant me: * impropérium exspectávit cor meum, et misériam.
<n>68:21</n> Et sustínui qui simul contristarétur, et non fuit: * et qui consolarétur, et non invéni.
<n>68:22</n> Et dedérunt in escam meam fel: * et in siti mea potavérunt me acéto.
<n>68:23</n> Fiat mensa eórum coram ipsis in láqueum, * et in retributiónes, et in scándalum.
<n>68:24</n> Obscuréntur óculi eórum ne vídeant: * et dorsum eórum semper incúrva.
<n>68:25</n> Effúnde super eos iram tuam: * et furor iræ tuæ comprehéndat eos.
<n>68:26</n> Fiat habitátio eórum desérta: * et in tabernáculis eórum non sit qui inhábitet.
<n>68:27</n> Quóniam quem tu percussísti, persecúti sunt: * et super dolórem vúlnerum meórum addidérunt.
<n>68:28</n> Appóne iniquitátem super iniquitátem eórum: * et non intrent in justítiam tuam.
<n>68:29</n> Deleántur de libro vivéntium: * et cum justis non scribántur.
06.1a470760b5:
<n>68:14</n> In the multitude of thy mercy hear me, * in the truth of thy salvation.
<n>68:15</n> Draw me out of the mire, that I may not stick fast: * deliver me from them that hate me, and out of the deep waters.
<n>68:16</n> Let not the tempest of water drown me, nor the deep swallow me up: * and let not the pit shut her mouth upon me.
<n>68:17</n> Hear me, O Lord, for thy mercy is kind; * look upon me according to the multitude of thy tender mercies.
<n>68:18</n> And turn not away thy face from thy servant: * for I am in trouble, hear me speedily.
<n>68:19</n> Attend to my soul, and deliver it: * save me because of my enemies.
<n>68:20</n> Thou knowest my reproach, and my confusion, * and my shame.
<n>68:21</n> In thy sight are all they that afflict me; * my heart hath expected reproach and misery.
<n>68:21</n> And I looked for one that would grieve together with me, * but there was none: and for one that would comfort me, and I found none.
<n>68:22</n> And they gave me gall for my food, * and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
<n>68:23</n> Let their table become as a snare before them, * and a recompense, and a stumblingblock.
<n>68:24</n> Let their eyes be darkened that they see not; * and their back bend thou down always.
<n>68:25</n> Pour out thy indignation upon them: * and let thy wrathful anger take hold of them.
<n>68:26</n> Let their habitation be made desolate: * and let there be none to dwell in their tabernacles.
<n>68:27</n> Because they have persecuted him whom thou hast smitten; * and they have added to the grief of my wounds.
<n>68:28</n> Add thou iniquity upon their iniquity: * and let them not come into thy justice.
<n>68:29</n> Let them be blotted out of the book of the living; * and with the just let them not be written.
06.a9ba84fff1:
<n>68:30</n> Ego sum pauper et dolens: * salus tua, Deus, suscépit me.
<n>68:31</n> Laudábo nomen Dei cum cántico: * et magnificábo eum in laude:
<n>68:32</n> Et placébit Deo super vítulum novéllum: * córnua producéntem et úngulas.
<n>68:33</n> Vídeant páuperes et læténtur: * quǽrite Deum, et vivet ánima vestra.
<n>68:34</n> Quóniam exaudívit páuperes Dóminus: * et vinctos suos non despéxit.
<n>68:35</n> Laudent illum cæli et terra, * mare et ómnia reptília in eis.
<n>68:36</n> Quóniam Deus salvam fáciet Sion: * et ædificabúntur civitátes Juda.
<n>68:36</n> Et inhabitábunt ibi, * et hereditáte acquírent eam.
<n>68:37</n> Et semen servórum ejus possidébit eam: * et qui díligunt nomen ejus, habitábunt in ea.
06.60d38b5092:
<n>68:30</n> I am poor and sorrowful: * thy salvation, O God, hath set me up.
<n>68:31</n> I will praise the name of God with a canticle: * and I will magnify him with praise.
<n>68:32</n> And it shall please God better than a young calf, * that bringeth forth horns and hoofs.
<n>68:33</n> Let the poor see and rejoice: * seek ye God, and your soul shall live.
<n>68:34</n> For the Lord hath heard the poor: * and hath not despised his prisoners.
<n>68:35</n> Let the heavens and the earth praise him; * the sea, and every thing that creepeth therein.
<n>68:36</n> For God will save Sion, * and the cities of Juda shall be built up.
<n>68:36</n> And they shall dwell there, * and acquire it by inheritance.
<n>68:37</n> And the seed of his servants shall possess it; * and they that love his name shall dwell therein.
06.c5bd27b57d:
<n>69:2</n> Deus, in adjutórium meum inténde: * Dómine, ad adjuvándum me festína.
<n>69:3</n> Confundántur et revereántur, * qui quærunt ánimam meam.
<n>69:4</n> Avertántur retrórsum, et erubéscant, * qui volunt mihi mala.
<n>69:4</n> Avertántur statim erubescéntes, * qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge.
<n>69:5</n> Exsúltent et læténtur in te omnes qui quærunt te, * et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus: qui díligunt salutáre tuum.
<n>69:6</n> Ego vero egénus, et pauper sum: * Deus, ádjuva me.
<n>69:6</n> Adjútor meus, et liberátor meus es tu: * Dómine, ne moréris.
06.845ce19046:
<n>69:2</n> O God, come to my assistance; * O Lord, make haste to help me.
<n>69:3</n> Let them be confounded and ashamed * that seek my soul:
<n>69:4</n> Let them be turned backward, and blush for shame * that desire evils to me:
<n>69:4</n> Let them be presently turned away blushing for shame * that say to me: ’T is well, ’t is well.
<n>69:5</n> Let all that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee; * and let such as love thy salvation say always: The Lord be magnified.
<n>69:6</n> But I am needy and poor; * O God, help me.
<n>69:6</n> Thou art my helper and my deliverer: * O Lord, make no delay.
06.f25b4cf6cf:
<n>63:2</n> Exáudi, Deus, oratiónem meam cum déprecor: * a timóre inimíci éripe ánimam meam.
<n>63:3</n> Protexísti me a convéntu malignántium: * a multitúdine operántium iniquitátem.
<n>63:4</n> Quia exacuérunt ut gládium linguas suas: * intendérunt arcum rem amáram, ut sagíttent in occúltis immaculátum.
<n>63:6</n> Súbito sagittábunt eum, et non timébunt: * firmavérunt sibi sermónem nequam.
<n>63:6</n> Narravérunt ut abscónderent láqueos: * dixérunt: Quis vidébit eos?
<n>63:7</n> Scrutáti sunt iniquitátes: * defecérunt scrutántes scrutínio.
<n>63:7</n> Accédet homo ad cor altum: * et exaltábitur Deus.
<n>63:8</n> Sagíttæ parvulórum factæ sunt plagæ eórum: * et infirmátæ sunt contra eos linguæ eórum.
<n>63:9</n> Conturbáti sunt omnes qui vidébant eos: * et tímuit omnis homo.
<n>63:10</n> Et annuntiavérunt ópera Dei, * et facta ejus intellexérunt.
<n>63:11</n> Lætábitur justus in Dómino, et sperábit in eo, * et laudabúntur omnes recti corde.
06.a0e10413ea:
<n>63:2</n> Hear, O God, my prayer, when I make supplication to thee: * deliver my soul from the fear of the enemy.
<n>63:3</n> Thou hast protected me from the assembly of the malignant; * from the multitude of the workers of iniquity.
<n>63:4</n> For they have whetted their tongues like a sword; * they have bent their bow a bitter thing, to shoot in secret the undefiled.
<n>63:6</n> They will shoot at him on a sudden, and will not fear: * they are resolute in wickedness.
<n>63:6</n> They have talked of hiding snares; * they have said: Who shall see them?
<n>63:7</n> They have searched after iniquities: * they have failed in their search.
<n>63:7</n> Man shall come to a deep heart: * and God shall be exalted.
<n>63:8</n> The arrows of children are their wounds: * and their tongues against them are made weak.
<n>63:9</n> All that saw them were troubled; * and every man was afraid.
<n>63:10</n> And they declared the works of God: * and understood his doings.
<n>63:11</n> The just shall rejoice in the Lord, and shall hope in him: * and all the upright in heart shall be praised.
06.574d679015:
<n>65:1</n> Jubiláte Deo, omnis terra, psalmum dícite nómini ejus: * date glóriam laudi ejus.
<n>65:3</n> Dícite Deo: Quam terribília sunt ópera tua, Dómine! * in multitúdine virtútis tuæ mentiéntur tibi inimíci tui.
<n>65:4</n> Omnis terra adóret te, et psallat tibi: * psalmum dicat nómini tuo.
<n>65:5</n> Veníte, et vidéte ópera Dei: * terríbilis in consíliis super fílios hóminum.
<n>65:6</n> Qui convértit mare in áridam, in flúmine pertransíbunt pede: * ibi lætábimur in ipso.
<n>65:7</n> Qui dominátur in virtúte sua in ætérnum, óculi ejus super gentes respíciunt: * qui exásperant non exalténtur in semetípsis.
<n>65:8</n> Benedícite, gentes, Deum nostrum: * et audítam fácite vocem laudis ejus,
<n>65:9</n> Qui pósuit ánimam meam ad vitam: * et non dedit in commotiónem pedes meos.
<n>65:10</n> Quóniam probásti nos, Deus: * igne nos examinásti, sicut examinátur argéntum.
<n>65:11</n> Induxísti nos in láqueum, posuísti tribulatiónes in dorso nostro: * imposuísti hómines super cápita nostra.
<n>65:12</n> Transívimus per ignem et aquam: * et eduxísti nos in refrigérium.
<n>65:13</n> Introíbo in domum tuam in holocáustis: * reddam tibi vota mea, quæ distinxérunt lábia mea.
<n>65:14</n> Et locútum est os meum, * in tribulatióne mea.
<n>65:15</n> Holocáusta medulláta ófferam tibi cum incénso aríetum: * ófferam tibi boves cum hircis.
<n>65:16</n> Veníte, audíte, et narrábo, omnes, qui timétis Deum: * quanta fecit ánimæ meæ.
<n>65:17</n> Ad ipsum ore meo clamávi, * et exaltávi sub lingua mea.
<n>65:18</n> Iniquitátem si aspéxi in corde meo, * non exáudiet Dóminus.
<n>65:19</n> Proptérea exaudívit Deus, * et atténdit voci deprecatiónis meæ.
<n>65:20</n> Benedíctus Deus, * qui non amóvit oratiónem meam, et misericórdiam suam a me.
06.db16498c56:
<n>65:1</n> Shout with joy to God, all the earth, sing ye a psalm to his name; * give glory to his praise.
<n>65:3</n> Say unto God, How terrible are thy works, O Lord! * in the multitude of thy strength thy enemies shall lie to thee.
<n>65:4</n> Let all the earth adore thee, * and sing to thee: let it sing a psalm to thy name.
<n>65:5</n> Come and see the works of God; * who is terrible in his counsels over the sons of men.
<n>65:6</n> Who turneth the sea into dry land, in the river they shall pass on foot: * there shall we rejoice in him.
<n>65:7</n> Who by his power ruleth for ever: his eyes behold the nations; * let not them that provoke him be exalted in themselves.
<n>65:8</n> O bless our God, ye Gentiles: * and make the voice of his praise to be heard.
<n>65:9</n> Who hath set my soul to live: * and hath not suffered my feet to be moved:
<n>65:10</n> For thou, O God, hast proved us: * thou hast tried us by fire, as silver is tried.
<n>65:11</n> Thou hast brought us into a net, thou hast laid afflictions on our back: * thou hast set men over our heads.
<n>65:12</n> We have passed through fire and water, * and thou hast brought us out into a refreshment.
<n>65:13</n> I will go into thy house with burnt offerings: * I will pay thee my vows, which my lips have uttered,
<n>65:14</n> And my mouth hath spoken, * when I was in trouble.
<n>65:15</n> I will offer up to thee holocausts full of marrow, with burnt offerings of rams: * I will offer to thee bullocks with goats.
<n>65:16</n> Come and hear, all ye that fear God, * and I will tell you what great things he hath done for my soul.
<n>65:17</n> I cried to him with my mouth: * and I extolled him with my tongue.
<n>65:18</n> If I have looked at iniquity in my heart, * the Lord will not hear me.
<n>65:19</n> Therefore hath God heard me, * and hath attended to the voice of my supplication.
<n>65:20</n> Blessed be God, * who hath not turned away my prayer, nor his mercy from me.

<n>68:28</n> Appóne iniquitátem super iniquitátem eórum: * et non intrent in justítiam tuam.
<n>68:29</n> Deleántur de libro vivéntium: * et cum justis non scribántur.
<n>68:30</n> Ego sum pauper et dolens: * salus tua, Deus, suscépit me.
<n>68:31</n> Laudábo nomen Dei cum cántico: * et magnificábo eum in laude:
<n>68:32</n> Et placébit Deo super vítulum novéllum: * córnua producéntem et úngulas.
<n>68:33</n> Vídeant páuperes et læténtur: * quǽrite Deum, et vivet ánima vestra.
<n>68:34</n> Quóniam exaudívit páuperes Dóminus: * et vinctos suos non despéxit.
<n>68:35</n> Laudent illum cæli et terra, * mare et ómnia reptília in eis.
<n>68:36</n> Quóniam Deus salvam fáciet Sion: * et ædificabúntur civitátes Juda.
<n>68:36</n> Et inhabitábunt ibi, * et hereditáte acquírent eam.
<n>68:37</n> Et semen servórum ejus possidébit eam: * et qui díligunt nomen ejus, habitábunt in ea.

<n>68:2</n> Save me, O God: * for the waters are come in even unto my soul.
<n>68:3</n> I stick fast in the mire of the deep: * and there is no sure standing.
<n>68:3</n> I am come into the depth of the sea: * and a tempest hath overwhelmed me.
<n>68:4</n> I have laboured with crying; my jaws are become hoarse: * my eyes have failed, whilst I hope in my God.
<n>68:5</n> They are multiplied above the hairs of my head, * who hate me without cause.
<n>68:5</n> My enemies are grown strong who have wrongfully persecuted me: * then did I pay that which I took not away.
<n>68:6</n> O God, thou knowest my foolishness; * and my offences are not hidden from thee.
<n>68:7</n> Let not them be ashamed for me, who look for thee, O Lord, * the Lord of hosts.
<n>68:7</n> Let them not be confounded on my account, * who seek thee, O God of Israel.
<n>68:8</n> Because for thy sake I have borne reproach; * shame hath covered my face.
<n>68:9</n> I am become a stranger to my brethren, * and an alien to the sons of my mother.
<n>68:10</n> For the zeal of thy house hath eaten me up: * and the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me.
<n>68:11</n> And I covered my soul in fasting: * and it was made a reproach to me.
<n>68:12</n> And I made haircloth my garment: * and I became a byword to them.
<n>68:13</n> They that sat in the gate spoke against me: * and they that drank wine made me their song.
<n>68:13</n> But as for me, my prayer is to thee, O Lord; * for the time of thy good pleasure, O God.
<n>68:14</n> In the multitude of thy mercy hear me, * in the truth of thy salvation.
<n>68:15</n> Draw me out of the mire, that I may not stick fast: * deliver me from them that hate me, and out of the deep waters.
<n>68:16</n> Let not the tempest of water drown me, nor the deep swallow me up: * and let not the pit shut her mouth upon me.
<n>68:17</n> Hear me, O Lord, for thy mercy is kind; * look upon me according to the multitude of thy tender mercies.
<n>68:18</n> And turn not away thy face from thy servant: * for I am in trouble, hear me speedily.
<n>68:19</n> Attend to my soul, and deliver it: * save me because of my enemies.
<n>68:20</n> Thou knowest my reproach, and my confusion, * and my shame.
<n>68:21</n> In thy sight are all they that afflict me; * my heart hath expected reproach and misery.
<n>68:21</n> And I looked for one that would grieve together with me, * but there was none: and for one that would comfort me, and I found none.
<n>68:22</n> And they gave me gall for my food, * and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
<n>68:23</n> Let their table become as a snare before them, * and a recompense, and a stumblingblock.
<n>68:24</n> Let their eyes be darkened that they see not; * and their back bend thou down always.
<n>68:25</n> Pour out thy indignation upon them: * and let thy wrathful anger take hold of them.
<n>68:26</n> Let their habitation be made desolate: * and let there be none to dwell in their tabernacles.
<n>68:27</n> Because they have persecuted him whom thou hast smitten; * and they have added to the grief of my wounds.
<n>68:28</n> Add thou iniquity upon their iniquity: * and let them not come into thy justice.
<n>68:29</n> Let them be blotted out of the book of the living; * and with the just let them not be written.
<n>68:30</n> I am poor and sorrowful: * thy salvation, O God, hath set me up.
<n>68:31</n> I will praise the name of God with a canticle: * and I will magnify him with praise.
<n>68:32</n> And it shall please God better than a young calf, * that bringeth forth horns and hoofs.
<n>68:33</n> Let the poor see and rejoice: * seek ye God, and your soul shall live.
<n>68:34</n> For the Lord hath heard the poor: * and hath not despised his prisoners.
<n>68:35</n> Let the heavens and the earth praise him; * the sea, and every thing that creepeth therein.
<n>68:36</n> For God will save Sion, * and the cities of Juda shall be built up.
<n>68:36</n> And they shall dwell there, * and acquire it by inheritance.
<n>68:37</n> And the seed of his servants shall possess it; * and they that love his name shall dwell therein.
06.ae5bd5b84a:
<n>67:2</n> Exsúrgat Deus, et dissipéntur inimíci ejus, * et fúgiant qui odérunt eum, a fácie ejus.
<n>67:3</n> Sicut déficit fumus, defíciant: * sicut fluit cera a fácie ignis, sic péreant peccatóres a fácie Dei.
<n>67:4</n> Et justi epuléntur, et exsúltent in conspéctu Dei: * et delecténtur in lætítia.
<n>67:5</n> Cantáte Deo, psalmum dícite nómini ejus: * iter fácite ei, qui ascéndit super occásum: <n>(fit reverentia)</n> Dóminus nomen illi.
<n>67:5</n> Exsultáte in conspéctu ejus: * turbabúntur a fácie ejus, patris orphanórum et júdicis viduárum.
<n>67:6</n> Deus in loco sancto suo: * Deus, qui inhabitáre facit uníus moris in domo:
<n>67:7</n> Qui edúcit vinctos in fortitúdine, * simíliter eos qui exásperant, qui hábitant in sepúlcris.
<n>67:8</n> Deus, cum egrederéris in conspéctu pópuli tui, * cum pertransíres in desérto:
<n>67:9</n> Terra mota est, étenim cæli distillavérunt a fácie Dei Sínai, * a fácie Dei Israël.
<n>67:10</n> Plúviam voluntáriam segregábis, Deus, hereditáti tuæ: * et infirmáta est, tu vero perfecísti eam.
<n>67:11</n> Animália tua habitábunt in ea: * parásti in dulcédine tua páuperi, Deus.
<n>67:12</n> Dóminus dabit verbum evangelizántibus, * virtúte multa.
<n>67:13</n> Rex virtútum dilécti, dilécti: * et speciéi domus divídere spólia.
<n>67:14</n> Si dormiátis inter médios cleros, pennæ colúmbæ deargentátæ, * et posterióra dorsi ejus in pallóre auri.
<n>67:15</n> Dum discérnit cæléstis reges super eam, nive dealbabúntur in Selmon: * mons Dei, mons pinguis.
<n>67:16</n> Mons coagulátus, mons pinguis: * ut quid suspicámini montes coagulátos?
<n>67:17</n> Mons, in quo beneplácitum est Deo habitáre in eo: * étenim Dóminus habitábit in finem.
<n>67:18</n> Currus Dei decem míllibus múltiplex, míllia lætántium: * Dóminus in eis in Sina in sancto.
<n>67:19</n> Ascendísti in altum, cepísti captivitátem: * accepísti dona in homínibus.
<n>67:19</n> Étenim non credéntes, * inhabitáre Dóminum Deum.
<n>67:20</n> Benedíctus Dóminus die cotídie: * prósperum iter fáciet nobis Deus salutárium nostrórum.
<n>67:21</n> Deus noster, Deus salvos faciéndi: * et Dómini Dómini éxitus mortis.
<n>67:22</n> Verúmtamen Deus confrínget cápita inimicórum suórum: * vérticem capílli perambulántium in delíctis suis.
<n>67:23</n> Dixit Dóminus: Ex Basan convértam, * convértam in profúndum maris:
<n>67:24</n> Ut intingátur pes tuus in sánguine: * lingua canum tuórum ex inimícis, ab ipso.
<n>67:25</n> Vidérunt ingréssus tuos, Deus: * ingréssus Dei mei: regis mei qui est in sancto.
<n>67:26</n> Prævenérunt príncipes conjúncti psalléntibus: * in médio juvenculárum tympanistriárum.
<n>67:27</n> In ecclésiis benedícite Deo Dómino, * de fóntibus Israël.
<n>67:28</n> Ibi Bénjamin adolescéntulus: * in mentis excéssu.
<n>67:28</n> Príncipes Juda, duces eórum: * príncipes Zábulon, príncipes Néphtali.
<n>67:29</n> Manda, Deus, virtúti tuæ: * confírma hoc, Deus, quod operátus es in nobis.
<n>67:30</n> A templo tuo in Jerúsalem, * tibi ófferent reges múnera.
<n>67:31</n> Íncrepa feras arúndinis, congregátio taurórum in vaccis populórum: * ut exclúdant eos, qui probáti sunt argénto.
<n>67:31</n> Díssipa gentes, quæ bella volunt: vénient legáti ex Ægýpto: * Æthiópia prævéniet manus ejus Deo.
<n>67:33</n> Regna terræ, cantáte Deo: * psállite Dómino.
<n>67:33</n> Psállite Deo, qui ascéndit super cælum cæli, * ad Oriéntem.
<n>67:34</n> Ecce dabit voci suæ vocem virtútis, date glóriam Deo super Israël, * magnificéntia ejus, et virtus ejus in núbibus.
<n>67:36</n> Mirábilis Deus in sanctis suis, Deus Israël ipse dabit virtútem, et fortitúdinem plebi suæ, * benedíctus Deus.
06.b45985ad52:
<n>67:2</n> Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered: * and let them that hate him flee from before his face.
<n>67:3</n> As smoke vanisheth, so let them vanish away: * as wax melteth before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God.
<n>67:4</n> And let the just feast, and rejoice before God: * and be delighted with gladness.
<n>67:5</n> Sing ye to God, sing a psalm to his name, * make a way for him who ascendeth upon the west: <n>(bow head)</n> the Lord is his name.
<n>67:5</n> Rejoice ye before him: * but the wicked shall be troubled at his presence, who is the father of orphans, and the judge of widows.
<n>67:6</n> God in his holy place: * God who maketh men of one manner to dwell in a house:
<n>67:7</n> Who bringeth out them that were bound in strength; * in like manner them that provoke, that dwell in sepulchres.
<n>67:8</n> O God, when thou didst go forth in the sight of thy people, * when thou didst pass through the desert:
<n>67:9</n> The earth was moved, and the heavens dropped at the presence of the God of Sinai, * at the presence of the God of Israel.
<n>67:10</n> Thou shalt set aside for thy inheritance a free rain, * O God: and it was weakened, but thou hast made it perfect.
<n>67:11</n> In it shall thy animals dwell; * in thy sweetness, O God, thou hast provided for the poor.
<n>67:12</n> The Lord shall give the word to them that preach good tidings, * with great power.
<n>67:13</n> The king of powers is of the beloved, * of the beloved; and the beauty of the house shall divide spoils.
<n>67:14</n> If you sleep among the midst of lots, you shall be as the wings of a dove covered with silver, * and the hinder parts of her back with the paleness of gold.
<n>67:15</n> When he that is in heaven appointeth kings over her, they shall be whited with snow in Selmon. * The mountain of God is a fat mountain,
<n>67:16</n> a curdled mountain, a fat mountain; * Why suspect, ye curdled mountains?
<n>67:17</n> A mountain in which God is well pleased to dwell: * for there the Lord shall dwell unto the end.
<n>67:18</n> The chariot of God is attended by ten thousands; thousands of them that rejoice: * the Lord is among them in Sinai, in the holy place.
<n>67:19</n> Thou hast ascended on high, thou hast led captivity captive; * thou hast received gifts in men.
<n>67:19</n> Yea for those also that do not believe, * the dwelling of the Lord God.
<n>67:20</n> Blessed be the Lord day by day: * the God of our salvation will make our journey prosperous to us.
<n>67:21</n> Our God is the God of salvation: * and of the Lord, of the Lord are the issues from death.
<n>67:22</n> But God shall break the heads of his enemies: * the hairy crown of them that walk on in their sins.
<n>67:23</n> The Lord said: I will turn them from Basan, * I will turn them into the depth of the sea:
<n>67:24</n> That thy foot may be dipped in the blood of thy enemies; * the tongue of thy dogs be red with the same.
<n>67:25</n> They have seen thy goings, O God, * the goings of my God: of my king who is in his sanctuary.
<n>67:26</n> Princes went before joined with singers, * in the midst of young damsels playing on timbrels.
<n>67:27</n> In the churches bless ye God the Lord, * from the fountains of Israel.
<n>67:28</n> There is Benjamin a youth, * in ecstasy of mind.
<n>67:28</n> The princes of Juda are their leaders: * the princes of Zabulon, the princes of Nephthali.
<n>67:29</n> Command thy strength, O God: * confirm, O God, what thou hast wrought in us.
<n>67:30</n> From thy temple in Jerusalem, * kings shall offer presents to thee.
<n>67:31</n> Rebuke the wild beasts of the reeds, the congregation of bulls with the kine of the people; * who seek to exclude them who are tried with silver.
<n>67:31</n> Scatter thou the nations that delight in wars: ambassadors shall come out of Egypt: * Ethiopia shall soon stretch out her hands to God.
<n>67:33</n> Sing to God, ye kingdoms of the earth: * sing ye to the Lord:
<n>67:33</n> Sing ye to God, who mounteth above the heaven of heavens, * to the east.
<n>67:34</n> Behold he will give to his voice the voice of power: give ye glory to God for Israel, * his magnificence, and his power is in the clouds.
<n>67:36</n> God is wonderful in his saints: the God of Israel is he who will give power and strength to his people; * blessed be God.
